previous.quote: In Zhang and Sternberg’s study, the mainland research participants rated intellectual styles as the most important resource for crea- tivity in their explicit evaluation of the six resources, while they indicated that intel- lectual styles would be the second most important resource when they evaluated the hypothetical cases. However, in the present study, whereas the Hong Kong partici- pants’ratings of boys were consistent with those in Zhang and Sternberg’s study, their ratings of girls were not.
previous.reason: The study set out to test whether two major types of findings from Zhang and Sternberg (2011a) replicated: (a) theory-practice discrepancies centred on intelligence and on intellectual styles, and (b) the gender gap in expectations. While the authors confirm the gender gap and find a smaller theory-practice gap on intelligence (stating later that the study 'largely replicated' the original findings), they explicitly contrast the girls' intellectual-style ratings in the hypothetical cases with Zhang and Sternberg (2011a), where intellectual style was the second most important resource across hypothetical cases but dropped to fourth/sixth for girls here. Under the codebook rules, when a tested finding is explicitly contrasted as differing from the original alongside other replicated findings, the outcome is 'mixed'.

decision.quote:
Fur-

thermore, the fact that this study largely replicated the ﬁ ndings obtained by Zhang

and Sternberg (2011a), particularly concerning the ﬁ ndings concerning the theory–

practice and gender gaps, suggests the people’s conceptions of creativity are com-

plex: not only do different people have different conceptions of creativity, but also
the same people may have varying conceptions of creativity under different circum-

stances such as when their conceptions are assessed via different testing formats and

536 L.-f. Zhang

when they are asked to evaluate people of different genders. Researchers should,

therefore, take such complexities into account when studying this topic.
